I read the test class and the `uniq` implementation. The question asks specifically about every execution of line 140 in the fallback branch.

From `uniq`:
- line 139 initializes `seen = []`
- line 140 is the outer loop header `for e in c:`
- line 146 appends the current element after checking prior elements
- Python also revisits the loop header after the final iteration, when the loop is exhausted

So at line 140 there are two kinds of moments:
1. before the first iteration body runs, immediately after `seen = []`
2. before later iterations, after some prior `seen.append(e)` calls
3. once more after loop completion

The candidate invariant is `len(seen) > 0`. This already fails by direct code reasoning in any fallback execution that reaches line 140 for the first time, because `seen` has just been initialized to the empty list on line 139 and nothing has been appended yet. Therefore `len(seen) == 0`, not `> 0`, at that first line-140 event.

The test suite contains many non-empty heterogeneous containers that force the fallback, so such a first line-140 event definitely occurs. It also contains `test_empty_container_no_iterations`, where after `seen = []`, the loop header is evaluated with no iterations at all, so line 140 is reached with `seen` still empty there as well.

That is enough to conclude the proposed invariant does not hold at every observed line-140 event.
